name: French Defense
blurb: Black answers 1.e4 with ...e6 and ...d5, building a solid pawn chain and attacking White's centre later. A good choice for patient players who like counterattacks.

ideas.e4 e6: Prepares ...d5, so Black can challenge e4 with a pawn that is already supported.
ideas.e4 e6 d4 d5: Now e4 is attacked. White has to defend it, trade it, or push past.
ideas.e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4: The Winawer. The bishop attacks the c3 knight, which is the piece defending e4.
ideas.e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5: Attacks d4, the base of White's pawn chain. In the French, Black usually hits the chain at its base.
ideas.e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3+: Black gives up the bishop for the knight, leaving White with doubled c-pawns.
ideas.e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3+ bxc3: The knight cannot use f6, because the e5 pawn covers it, so it goes to e7 and later to f5 or c6.
Instead of guarding g7, Black attacks the e5 pawn and gets ready to take on d4.
Gains time by attacking the queen, and the rook now works on the open g-file.
ideas.e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 c5: Against the Tarrasch, Black strikes at d4 straight away. The d2 knight does not attack d5, so this is a good moment.
ideas.e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5: Against the Advance, the same plan: attack the base of the chain at d4.
ideas.e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6: Adds a second attacker to d4.
ideas.e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6: The queen attacks b2 and adds pressure on d4 from behind the c5 pawn.
ideas.e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 a3 c4: Gains space on the queenside and takes the b3 and d3 squares away from White's pieces.
ideas.e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5: Recapturing with the pawn opens the c8 bishop's diagonal, which the e6 pawn had blocked.
